claims.text: Progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading in FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers is governed by interface-mediated dislocation nucleation and accumulation.
Severe lattice distortion hinders dislocation glide within the layer interiors.
Local short-range order hinders dislocation glide within the layer interiors.
Hindered intralayer glide causes dislocations to be generated at and accumulate along FCC/BCC interfaces.
Dislocation accumulation at the interfaces progressively weakens those interfaces.
Progressive interface weakening produces enhanced creep relative to a state with less severe glide barriers.
The starting coating consists of alternating nanoscale FCC and BCC high-entropy-alloy layers.
The as-deposited or as-processed multilayer has significant lattice distortion and pronounced short-range order.
Post-deposition annealing or a compositional change can reduce interfacial short-range order and lattice distortion while preserving the multilayer architecture.
Testing at approximately 0.4–0.6 Tm can activate dislocation motion without causing full microstructural recovery.
FCC/BCC interfaces are the principal sites of dislocation nucleation and pile-up in the proposed deformation process.
Compositional complexity impedes conventional dislocation glide within individual layers.
The multilayer architecture directs dislocations toward the interfaces.
Reducing interfacial short-range order through annealing or compositional modification mitigates interfacial dislocation pile-up.
A treated multilayer with reduced interfacial short-range order and lattice distortion will exhibit a lower creep rate than the untreated baseline.
The treated multilayer will exhibit less progressive plastic deformation over an equivalent test duration than the untreated baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies only while deformation is dislocation-dominated, diffusion or recovery does not dominate, and the nanoscale multilayer structure remains intact.
Statistically indistinguishable creep rates and interfacial dislocation behavior between the modified and baseline samples would falsify the proposed controlling mechanism.
